headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when untrusted document-processing outputs feed a game-playing agent with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent B can read files, browse, and process documents, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content by default. Agent A is a game-playing component with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so if B forwards content into A’s pipeline, prompt-like instructions could be misread. The pairwise bridge is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests untrusted files or web pages and forwards their text to agent_a
IF the orchestrator copies B outputs into A inputs without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from B to A for any untrusted text
Add a provenance tag to every B output before A consumes it
Restrict B to allowlisted input sources only
Insert a human review step before A acts on B-generated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and filesystem access, while agent A has no network egress and no touched data classes. If both share a workspace, B could read and transmit files that A produces or stores locally. The profiles do not document a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced, but the leakage path is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF agent_a writes artifacts into a directory readable by agent_b
IF agent_b is allowed to upload local files or context to external APIs
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories with OS permissions
Disable B network egress for runs that touch sensitive files
Mount A outputs read-only for B
Scan B inputs for secrets before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; agent A has no documented write or coordination controls. If both operate on the same directory, B’s mutable actions can overwrite or race with A’s artifacts. Because no locking or isolation is documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share any writable directory
IF agent_b modifies files that agent_a also reads or writes
mitigations: Give each agent a separate working directory
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Make A outputs immutable before B starts
Run B with a read-only mount when possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s document-processing stack can treat upstream text as input, and agent A can generate outputs that B may consume. No verification or critique loop is documented between them, so A’s outputs could be propagated into B’s downstream actions or reports. The blast radius is limited by the lack of explicit action authority in A, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as authoritative inputs
IF B renders or acts on A-generated text without validation
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source data
Add a checksum or schema check before B consumes A output
Log and review any A-to-B handoff
Block direct action-taking from unverified A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and has no network egress; agent B’s docs list general multimodal processing but no regulated-data commitments. With no evidence of a compliance mismatch, the pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data under a conflicting policy
mitigations: Confirm both agents’ retention settings before deployment
Keep regulated data out of this pair unless policies are documented
Record residency and DPA requirements for any future rollout
